newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says summit with Arafat when deal near.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says summit with Arafat when deal near.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday he would meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat when negotiations on implementing a Hebron deal were near completion, and that was not the case yet.
"I said from the start in Washington Arafat and I would meet when talks are nearing conclusion," Netanyahu told reporters at parliament.
"So far, we have not set a time for such a meeting so you can assess where we are on the basis of that," he said.

PLO officials said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat rejected a proposal by Netanyahu that they could hold a summit on Monday if Arafat agreed to change the Hebron deal signed a year ago by Israel's previous government and give Israel powers in areas that were to be given to the PLO.
Israel and the PLO on Sunday delayed for at least one day formal talks on Hebron, set to reconvene on Monday in the Egyptian resort of Taba, to see if other channels might bear fruit.

The Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron should have been carried out in March but was delayed by the previous Israeli government in the wake of Islamic militant suicide bombings that killed 59 people in Israel in March and February.

It was frozen by Netanyahu, who won Israel's May elections. He is demanding changes in the deal which he says are necessary to ensure the security of some 400 Jewish settlers who live amidst 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron.
